title: An Inexpensive Way to Record and Quantify Bacterial Swarming
protocol: Setup the Yaheetech hydroponic tent according to the instruction manual.
Assemble the skeleton first and then cover it with the polyester material.
Use M5 bolts and nuts to assemble the camera frame as illustrated in figure 1.
Connect the Zinc-plated slotted angles first and then the aluminum bars.
Drill holes by the ends of the aluminum bars with hand drill or table drill for stabilization.
Cut the sides of 18’’ x 18’’ acrylic sheets slightly to fit in the sample platform using an acrylic cutter.
Use a circular cutter to cut a circle 9 inches in diameter out of one of the 18’’ x 18’’ acrylic sheets “A” from the center and leave the other uncut.
Fix sheet “A” on the sample platform.
Drill appropriate holes on the side to allow bolts to go through all the way down to the holes of slotted angles.
Fix the camera on the camera fixer with its lens facing downwards.
Adjust the fixer back and forth to align the camera with the circle on the acrylic sheet.
Tape the LED strip around the sample platform 1 inch above the acrylic sheet on the slotted angle.
Cut two pieces of black cloth, each approximately 20 inches by 20 inches in size.
Place one piece of black cloth on the bottom of the tent as a photography background.
Cut a hole in the center of the second piece of black cloth to allow the camera lens through and hang it onto the camera platform to shield reflections from above.
Place the camera stand inside the tent.
Load batteries for the LCD timer remote control.
Connect the LCD timer remote control with the camera through the hole on the top of the tent.
Tighten the hole using an elastic cord.
Cut circles out of three acrylic sheets, each with diameters of 9.2 cm, 5.75 inches, and 9.5 inches respectively.
Drill ¼ inch holes in each corner of the circles, 3 cm from both edges.
Assemble the light shield according to specifications.
Place the circular fluorescent light bulb between level I and the sample platform.
Stick the starter ballast under the sample platform using tapes.
Fix metal spring clamps on the sample platform if present, and clamp the bulb.
Put the heat control module inside the tent on the side of the bottom to avoid showing in photos.
Adjust the temperature setting to the desired temperature for swarming assays.
Set the humidifier outside the tent.
Connect the power cord to the humidity controller outlet.
Extend the extractable plastic mist tube through the hole on the tent wall into the tent beneath the sample platform.
Fill the humidifier tank with water.
Plug in the humidity controller to the power strip and adjust the humidity value according to the controller manual.
Place a 500 ml beaker under the mist tube to collect water droplets from the mist tube.
Fix the AC fan on one of the slotted angle legs facing the beaker using bolts and nuts that come with the fan.
Tighten all holes and seal the zip of the tent.
Weigh 0.5 g yeast extract, 1 g tryptone, and 0.5 g NaCl in a 100 mL Pyrex bottle.
Measure 100 mL deionized water and pour it into the bottle.
Close the lid and shake the bottle until all powders dissolve in water.
Loosen the bottle lid and place it in an autoclavable tray containing a thin layer of water.
Autoclave the LB broth for 25 minutes under 15 psi pressure and 121°C.
Transfer 5 mL of cooled LB broth to a 14 mL tube using pipet aid in the hood.
Remove bacteria glycerol stock from -80°C freezer.
Use a sterilized wood stick to scratch and transfer bacterial content into the LB broth.
Return glycerol stock to freezer.
Shake inoculated LB broth overnight at 37°C with shaking frequency of 200 rpm.
Weigh 0.5 g yeast extract, 1.0 g tryptone, 0.5 g NaCl, and 0.5 g agar into a 100 mL Pyrex bottle.
Measure 100 ml deionized water and add it to the bottle.
Place magnetic stir bar in the bottle.
Loosely close lid and place on hot plate magnetic stirrer.
Turn on the heat and the magnetic stirrer.
Wait for 10 - 15 minutes until the medium boils.
Turn off the stirring and heating after boiling begins.
Wear thermos-insulate gloves to transfer the bottle to an autoclavable tray with a thin layer of water.
Loosen the bottle lid and start autoclaving for 25 minutes under 15 psi, 121 °C.
Once autoclaving is complete, place the bottle back on the magnetic stirrer without heating but with stirring to cool down to 40~50 °C.
Set a flame when the target temperature is reached and use a pipet aid to transfer LB agar medium to 6 petri dishes, with 15 ml per dish.
Turn off the flame and wait for the agar to solidify, which takes about 2 hours.
(Optional) Use the freshly made plates or store inverted swarming plates in a 4 °C cold room for up to 2 days.
Remove the lid of swarming plates in the hood.
Dry the plates for 20 minutes when room humidity is above 50%RH.
Dry the plates for 10 minutes when room humidity is below 30%RH.
Adjust drying time accordingly between 10-20 minutes if room humidity is between 30-50%RH.
Do not over-dry the plates to prevent bacterial swarming issues due to surface friction or dryness.
Inoculate 2 μL overnight bacteria suspension on the center of a swarm plate using micropipette.
Transfer the swarm plates into the incubator after inoculation drop dried (3D hemisphere turns to a 2D circle).
Put one swarm plate inverted on the plate holder for time-lapse photography.
Turn on the fluorescent light bulb and camera when setting up for time-lapse photo.
Adjust position of acrylic sheets by rotating nuts on threaded rod, ensuring distance between sample platform and Level I is about 1.5 inches.
Ensure distance between Level I and Level II is slightly under 1 inch (about 2 cm), while Level II and Level III are separated by 3.5 inches for proper lighting setup.
Slightly lift or lower Level III to adjust the light intensity on the petri dish until it appears properly illuminated in camera preview.
Set the camera focal length to 35 mm - 65 mm.
Adjust the zoom ring to have the sample occupy the full screen but not exceed the border.
Use “M” manual mode to focus on the bacteria colony.
Set the aperture to F5.6 -F7.1.
Adjust the shutter speed until the resultant exposure value is 0 or -⅓.
Remove the light shield for multi-plate assay.
Turn on the LED light strip and place the uncut acrylic sheet on the sample platform.
Place swarm plates inverted on the acrylic sheet so that water will not condensate on the lid.
Check the camera preview to ensure all plates are within the range of the screen.
(Optional) Adjust the white balance to add more blue tone if the image appears too yellowish.
Set the frame rate and frame number of the LCD camera timer control according to the manual.
Press “start” button to start time-lapse photo shooting.
Seal the zip of the tent.
Make sure there is enough water in the humidifier water tank.
Gently open the window on top of tent to check condition inside without disturbing photographing.
Stop the timer controller when swarming is finished.
Connect camera with a laptop using USB data wire and download images to designated folder.
Detach laptop from the camera.
Check brightness variation in images and use “Stack Deflicker” plugin in ImageJ to calibrate brightness if necessary.
Check sample position variation over time in images and apply “Image Stabilizer” plugin to fix it if necessary.
Import the images using “File” -- “Import” -- “Image Sequence.”
Set the frame rate for animations via “Image” -- “Stacks” -- “Animations” -- “Animation options.”
Save the image sequence as an AVI file.
Drag the image of interest to the ImageJ control bar.
Calibrate the ratio of pixels to actual length using “Analyze” -- “Set Scale.”
Outline the colony edge with the freehand selection tool and press “M” to calculate the area.
Open the python script and change the file directory to where the image sequences are stored.
Run the python script to automatically calculate swarming speed and save data in a .txt file.
